section: Act II: Findings 6-10 (simulation results), report_public.md lines 168-266

claims.claim: 1,010,000 simulated maps; 4 independent chains x 252,500 steps
Base seed derived from drand beacon (League of Entropy)
Same 4,765 voting areas
Each new district kept within +/-12.5% of equal; Act allows +/-25%
claims.found: 'balanced to +/-12.5% at the proposal step (the Act allo[ws +/-25%])'; ReCom epsilon = pop_deviation/2

claims.claim: Every district in one piece (contiguous)
Official Elections Alberta shapefiles place the two commission maps among the plans
Percentile = share of neutral maps the real map outscores
claims.note: method definition; midrank vs strict differ only at ties (see 2019 row)

claims.claim: 2026 commission maps each have 89 districts
Neutral maps have 87 districts, the 2019 map's count
Panel's new map has 91 districts
Percentages are seat shares, which put three sizes on one scale, though not perfectly
claims.note: framing; AC C22 notes seats@50/50 takes k/87 values in the plans, which the report concedes

claims.claim: Size-matched check dated October 30, provisional, finds the same tilt
claims.found: Date 2026-10-30 19:10 MDT; 'provisional'; minority mean-median beyond almost every same-size plan; seats@50/50 46/89 matched or beaten by 0 (A), 124 (B), 263 (C), 905 (D) plans

claims.claim: A size-matched joint number has not reported
claims.found: No size-matched joint score for the minority found; joint_outlier.json scores the panel map against the 87-district canonical ensemble only
claims.note: absence claim; searched findings/ and data/outputs

claims.claim: Median neutral map gives UCP 44.8% of seats at an exactly even vote
Rural UCP voters win ridings by wide 60-40 margins; urban NDP voters win by tighter 51-49 margins
claims.found: 'Rural UCP-winning margins average 43.0 pp; urban NDP-winning margins average 21.5 pp' (about 71-29 and 61-39)
claims.note: The 60-40 and 51-49 figures are in no source. The same source says UCP is the MORE packed party (surplus-vote rate 15.9% vs NDP 9.3%) and the NDP deficit comes from dispersed losing votes in rural/suburban ridings, which contradicts the 'rural UCP wastes votes' explanation of the baseline.

claims.claim: Natural geography mildly favours the NDP's seat efficiency (baseline below 50%)
claims.found: median 44.8% UCP seats at 50/50 supports the direction
claims.note: numeric direction verified; the causal explanation is the line above and is contradicted by AC L967

claims.claim: Heading: Fewer than 100 maps in 1,010,000
2019 enacted: 46.0% UCP seats at 50/50
2019 map: 78th percentile
claims.note: Rounds to 79 if rounded; truncated to 78. Academic report says p78.54

claims.claim: 2019 map: 65th percentile once tied maps counted
Majority 2026: 46.1% UCP seats at 50/50
Majority: 78th percentile
claims.note: same rounding note; AC L1663: majority p78.54 is the upper edge of the 40/87 block

claims.claim: Minority 2026: 51.7% (46 seats)
Minority: 99.99th percentile
Fewer than 100 of 1,010,000 neutral draws reach this
Neutral median 44.8%
95th percentile 48.3%
99th percentile 49.4%
Maximum 51.72%
69 of 1,010,000 plans exceed the minority map's 51.69%
Million plans worth about 1,400 independent draws

claims.claim: Allowing for that, minority sits above at least the 98th percentile
Mean-median: deeper in tail than 99.97 per cent of neutral maps
Declination: deeper than 98.8 per cent
All of them lean toward the UCP
claims.found: minority EG +0.0402, MM +0.0104, decl +0.0770, s50 0.5169, all in UCP-favouring tail

claims.claim: Replay of 2023 election-day vote: minority map gives UCP 60 of 89 seats
claims.note: election-day basis, as labelled. Under Amendment 12 (all ballots; findings/allballots_ranking/README.md) the counts are minority 55, majority 48. All ballots is now the registered substrate, so 60/55 is a sensitivity figure.

claims.claim: Majority map: 55 of 89 on the same vote
claims.note: all-ballots value is 48 (see above)

claims.claim: Election-day vote leaned more UCP than the full count
claims.found: 2019 map: election-day 57 UCP / 30 NDP vs 2023 result 49 / 38

claims.claim: Hill-climbing is the standard tool for exploring biased-but-legal maps (Cannon et al. 2022)
claims.found: Cannon, Goldbloom-Helzner, Gupta, Matthews, Suwal (2023), 'Voting Rights, Markov Chains, and Optimization by Short Bursts', arXiv:2011.02288
claims.note: Academic report dates it 2023 throughout; public report says 2022. Align the year (journal version: Methodology and Computing in Applied Probability, 2023; arXiv 2020).

claims.claim: 40,000 steps each way, same constraints, same geometry
claims.found: 800 bursts x 50 steps = 40,000; UCP and NDP directions

claims.claim: Neutral maximum 51.72% at 50/50
Neutral minimum 37.9% at 50/50
claims.note: findings/burst_symmetry_analysis.md and AC H9 give a neutral floor of 39.08%, but that is the 250k v0_9 ensemble. On the canonical 1.01M it is 37.93%, identical to the NDP hill-climb value in the next rows, so the NDP-direction search adds nothing beyond the neutral floor.

claims.claim: Hill-climb UCP-maximising reaches 52.9%
claims.note: 46 of 87 seats; different denominator from the minority's 46/89 (AC C22)

claims.claim: Hill-climb NDP-maximising reaches 37.9%
Minority 51.7% closer to UCP ceiling (52.9) than neutral median (44.8)
Fine-grained sweep: minority keeps UCP at or above the 45-seat majority threshold down to about 49.2% of two-party vote
claims.found: 'the minority map keeps the UCP at 45 seats down to about 49.2% of the two-party vote (the site said 49.7%)'
claims.note: No raw sweep output file located in findings/ or data/outputs; verified only through the DOCUMENTED CORRECTIONS ledger. Site (viewer en.ts L788) still says 49.7% and 4 points.

claims.claim: UCP could lose it by about 1.6 points and still form government
claims.note: consistent as a margin (0.8 points of share)

claims.claim: On the majority map the UCP would need to win by about 9 points
claims.found: 'on the majority map the UCP needs to win by about 9 points (the site said 4)'
claims.note: ledger does not say whether 9 is margin or share

claims.claim: Neutral processes essentially never produce this map; majority is the kind a neutral procedure turns out all the time; minority is the kind you have to set out to draw
claims.note: framing; note 69 neutral plans do exceed it, and AC L1604 says the DPG-era 'set out to draw' framing does not hold on official geometry

claims.claim: Ensemble outlier analysis is the state of the art in redistricting statistics
claims.note: characterisation

claims.claim: Method US courts found persuasive in state cases that struck maps down
claims.found: League of Women Voters v. Commonwealth, 178 A.3d 737 (Pa. 2018): 'MGGG-style ensemble evidence carried weight'
claims.note: secondhand; the case itself is not in evidence/law/

claims.claim: Three of four metrics in the extreme tail, all four leaning the same way
claims.found: MM p99.97, decl p98.79, s50 p99.99; EG p94.54 same direction

claims.claim: 2019 map's highest placement on any partisan measure is in the low 90s
claims.note: true of the four registered measures. findings/extended_partisan_metrics_canonical.json lists a fifth measure (partisan_bias) for 2019 at p99.31, so 'any' holds only for the four

claims.claim: Minority sits at the 99.99th percentile against the naturally skewed baseline
No Canadian commission has ever been required to test its map against a neutral ensemble
claims.note: searched report_academic.md, analysis/methodology, evidence/law; nothing asserts or refutes it. AC L303 discusses commissions vs legislatures only

claims.claim: As far as this audit's review found, no Canadian court has yet weighed ensemble evidence
claims.note: hedged by 'as far as this audit's review found'; nothing in evidence/law/ contradicts it

claims.claim: Rucho v. Common Cause (2019): partisan gerrymandering claims are not for federal courts to police
claims.found: 'partisan gerrymandering claims present political questions beyond the reach of the federal courts'
claims.note: 'even strong statistical evidence' is the report's gloss; the opinion recites plaintiffs' simulations (24,518 plans) and partisan-asymmetry measures and still holds the claims nonjusticiable, so the gloss is fair

claims.claim: Ensemble respects population limits and contiguity but not s.15(2) hybrid protections, community of interest, municipal anchoring
claims.found: 'canonical ReCom run disables the s.15(2) rural-protection freeze'
claims.note: only s.15(2) is explicitly stated; the others follow from the method

claims.claim: Real electorate is not frozen at 50/50; the test isolates what the map adds
Efficiency gap for minority is +4.0%, 94.5th percentile
claims.note: election-day basis

claims.claim: Pre-registered outlier line is the 95th percentile, about +4.1%
claims.note: election-day basis

claims.claim: The efficiency gap missed the line ('It missed ... every table in this report shows it that way')
claims.found: Amendment 12 (2026-11-07) makes all ballots the registered substrate: P1 threshold becomes +1.39%; minority EG +2.55% is above it and its partisan lane moves from 3 of 4 to 4 of 4. Matched all-ballots ranking: minority EG p98.82 (election-day p94.54)
claims.note: The election-day miss stands as a sensitivity (Amendment 12 Part 4), but 'it stays a miss' is no longer the registered outcome. Lines 219 and 377 repeat the framing.

claims.claim: Majority efficiency gap +0.1%, 16.5th percentile
claims.note: election-day; all-ballots: -2.70%, p26.48

claims.claim: On its own, the EG miss shows almost nothing
EG's proposed US threshold about 7% is an academic proposal no court has adopted

claims.claim: No Canadian body uses the efficiency gap at all
claims.note: AC L1082 says the 7% figure 'appears in neither the EBCA nor any Canadian redistribution jurisprudence' (narrower); the 'no body at all' claim is unsourced

claims.claim: The threshold was set before the answer was known (locked line)
claims.found: Option D line 4.10% registered before official shapefiles

claims.claim: Combined four-metric profile bounded at about one in 568,000

Doubling covers the second analytical channel; Fisher combination not used

claims.claim: The two channels are not independent: both read the same 2023 votes
claims.found: Fisher independence check 'does not measure dependence between test statistics'; channels share the 2023 substrate

claims.claim: Four measures inside the simulation count as one look (folded into a joint score)

claims.claim: Third attack, mechanism test: the claim that Act I geometry is the mechanism for the Act II seat advantage failed its falsification test
claims.note: no committed result found stating that a test of 'geometry is the mechanism' failed. Searched report_academic.md (mechanism/falsif), findings/, the amendment log. Nearest: AC L967 says the Chen-Rodden urban-packing mechanism fails in Alberta (a different mechanism)

claims.claim: Link path findings/redist_python_comparison.md
Robustness across samplers separates finding from artifact; publishing a failed falsification separates audit from advocacy
Nobody requires any of this; the audit imposed it on itself, in writing, before running it

claims.claim: Neighbour-drain: minority 1 coupled chain signal vs majority's 2 and 2019 enacted 5
claims.found: 'minority 1 coupled chain signal, majority 2 and 2019 enacted 5'

claims.claim: A genuine pre-registered PASS; the single test where the minority numerically beats the majority
claims.found: 'The pre-registered PASS for the minority is unchanged under either count'
claims.note: tension: the registered S5 structural test (Amendment 5, Part 7) is also a neighbour-drain score, and the minority (0.0006) falls below the 0.0039 line, which flags it. Same name, different test. 'Single test' was not independently checked

claims.claim: Section 5.3.5 of the academic report explains the pass is real but narrow: the minority gets its partisan effect through hybridization (splitting cities into mixed urban/rural districts)
claims.found: 'Hybridization reading (dropped ...)' ... 'The test cannot show that, and the premises have since gone ... The "pack-and-hybridize versus pack-and-drain" label is not used.'
claims.note: Section 5.3.5 exists but it DROPS the hybridization explanation; the report credits it with the opposite of what it says

claims.claim: Packing and cracking happen within districts, not between them, so an adjacency test cannot see it
claims.note: this was the earlier draft's argument, since withdrawn

claims.claim: SZAT looked significant (p = 0.0024) until null corrected for spatial clustering
After correction SZAT returns p about 0.19, not significant
SZAT retired to exploratory status on 2026-06-13
claims.found: 'Block-permutation null (added 2026-06-13) ... SZAT is therefore retired as a confirmatory channel'

claims.claim: Fisher combination of the two channels assumes independence they lack and is not used
Retired tests suggested boundary choices were partisan-loaded; after correction nothing
Neighbours voting alike (spatial autocorrelation) is the classic way redistricting statistics mislead
claims.note: method commentary; Moran's I = 0.7534 (plain_language_defense.md L592) supports the underlying fact

claims.claim: A drain-test pass beside tail results is a fingerprint of which mechanism the map does not use
Two of these were the audit's own instruments failing, the third points in the map's favour
'Two retired, one pass for the other side'
